backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, pick a random point in the square, take the 3 circles whose centres are nearest to it, and re-seed all 3 at random positions inside the disc of radius 0.15 around that point with radius 0. Then run _optimise from there and accept if the repaired sum improves. This operates on a local cluster and gives a different neighbourhood from single-circle reinsertion.
backlog.title: Localised region destroy-and-rebuild

backlog.spec: After the remove-and-reinsert loop and before returning, run one more SLSQP from the best (c, r) with maxiter 1000 and options ftol=1e-12. Do this only if at least 1.5 s of the 30 s remains, measured from t0 with process_time. Clip, repair, and keep the result only if its repaired sum is higher. This recovers the slack that the 200-iteration cap and the default ftol leave in the final packing, which the 1e-9 repair shrink cannot.
backlog.title: Final convergence polish of the returned packing

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, count consecutive steps without improvement. If the count reaches 60, save the current packing into an elite list if it is the best seen, then start a fresh random restart with _solve_once and _repair, and continue reinsertion from that new packing. Keep the global best across all restarts as the returned result. This is an iterated local search with restarts triggered by stagnation rather than a fixed phase length.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered full restart with global elite memory

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run two SLSQP solves instead of one. The first, with maxiter 80, minimises -sum(r) + LAMBDA * n * var(r) with LAMBDA = 0.5 under the same constraints, which discourages solutions with a few tiny circles squeezed among large ones. The second is the existing _optimise call (true objective, MAX_ITER iterations) warm-started from the first result. Implement by giving _optimise an optional lam argument (default 0) and maxiter argument. The reinsertion loop keeps using the true objective only.
backlog.title: Variance-penalised objective in the first pass of each restart

backlog.spec: In the random-restart phase, after each restart's SLSQP solve and repair, run 3 remove-smallest-and-reinsert steps on that packing straight away. Reuse the same code as the main loop (factor it into a helper _reinsert_step(c, r, rng) that returns the better of old and new). Only then compare the result with best. This ranks restarts by their quality after a little refinement rather than as raw output, so promising basins are not thrown away early. Keep RESTART_FRACTION at 0.3, and the main reinsertion loop continues from the chosen best.
backlog.title: Mini reinsertion polish inside each restart

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, instead of drawing the new centre of the removed circle uniformly over the square, pick a random remaining circle k, then draw the new centre uniformly in a disc of radius 0.15 around c[k], clipped to [0, 1]^2. Keep r = 0, the same _optimise, _repair, and accept rule. The move then stays in the same local region of the packing rather than jumping across it.
backlog.title: Neighbourhood-local reinsertion site

backlog.spec: After the random-restart phase, use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 2n centre coordinates in [0,1]^(2n), with the energy being the negative sum of greedily repaired radii for those centres (radii set by the pairwise and wall-distance maximum-feasible rule, computed in numpy). Give dual_annealing maxiter and seed=rng.integers(2**31) and stop it when the time budget is used up, using a callback or a fixed small maxiter that fits the remaining time. Polish the best centres found with _optimise and _repair, and keep the better of this and the restart best.
backlog.title: Dual-annealing outer search over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Replace the strict-improvement acceptance in the remove-and-reinsert loop with late-acceptance hill climbing. Keep a circular history list of length L = 10 initialised with the current sum of radii, a current packing and a separate best packing. At step k, accept the repaired candidate into current if its sum is at least the current sum or at least history[k % L]; then set history[k % L] to the current sum. Update best whenever current exceeds it and return best at the end. This needs no temperature parameter and lets the search walk across plateaus and through slightly worse packings.
backlog.title: Late-acceptance hill climbing in the reinsertion loop

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, replace the choice of the smallest circle with a cyclic index: at step t, remove and reinsert circle t mod n, using the same uniform random reinsertion, _optimise, _repair, and accept-if-better rule. Each full pass of n steps then visits every circle exactly once, which makes coverage systematic rather than biased toward small radii.
backlog.title: Cyclic round-robin removal of each circle

backlog.spec: Change RESTART_FRACTION from 0.3 to 0.1, so about 2.4 s goes to random SLSQP restarts and about 21.6 s goes to the remove-and-reinsert loop, which was the source of the only accepted gain. No other change. The 'or best is None' guard in the first while loop stays, so at least one restart always completes.
backlog.title: Shorten the random-restart phase to 10 percent

backlog.spec: Change _optimise to run SLSQP first with maxiter=60 and ftol=1e-6, and then continue from that point with maxiter=200 and ftol=1e-9 only if the loose sum of radii (after clipping) is within 0.01 of the current best sum. Weak restarts are then dropped cheaply, so more restarts and reinsertion steps fit in the time budget. Pass the current best sum as an optional argument.
backlog.title: Two-stage loose-then-tight SLSQP

backlog.spec: As the perturbation in the reinsertion loop, pick a random 25 percent of circles and multiply their radii by 0.5 while keeping every centre fixed. Then run _optimise from that point with all centres and radii free, followed by _repair, and accept under the usual rule that the repaired sum must beat the incumbent. Use the same loop and time budget as the original code, and do not change the removal step.
backlog.title: Radius destroy-and-regrow kick

backlog.spec: Add a second move type to the reinsertion loop, used with probability 0.5. Pick a random circle i among the 8 smallest. Find its two nearest neighbours a and b by gap (centre distance minus the two radii). Reflect the centre of i across the straight line through the centres of a and b, so that it lands in the pocket on the other side of that pair; clip the new centre to [0.01, 0.99] and set r_i to 0. Then call _optimise, clip, repair and accept if the sum improves, as now. With the other probability 0.5 keep the existing remove-smallest uniform reinsertion. Use rng for all random choices.
backlog.title: Reflection flip move across a contact pair

backlog.spec: Apply three previously near-miss changes together on top of the current script. (a) In _solve_once, draw the initial centres as a Latin hypercube sample: for each of the two coordinates, take a random permutation of the n strata of [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and add uniform jitter inside each stratum. (b) In _optimise, pass analytic derivatives to SLSQP: the objective gradient is 0 for centre variables and -1 for radii; the constraint Jacobian is a dense (n(n-1)/2 + 5n, 3n) array with unit-vector entries (c_i-c_j)/d (d clamped to at least 1e-12) for pair rows, -1 for both radii in pair rows, +-1 and -1 for wall rows, and +1 for the r>=0 rows. (c) In the remove-and-reinsert loop, keep a separate current packing and best packing; accept a worse candidate into current with probability exp(delta/T), where T decays linearly from 0.002 to 0 over the remaining time budget; always return best. Keep _repair and all else unchanged.
backlog.title: Combine LHS starts, annealed acceptance and analytic Jacobians

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, before calling _optimise on the candidate, multiply all radii of the other n-1 circles by a factor drawn uniformly from [0.85, 0.97] (the reinserted circle keeps radius 0). This starts SLSQP from a strictly interior point with free room around every circle, so its first steps can rearrange centres instead of being pinned by the active contact set of the current jammed packing. The acceptance test still compares the repaired candidate sum against the unscaled current sum. No other change.
backlog.title: Slack warm start for reinsertion solves

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, after choosing the random new centre p for the smallest circle, find all circles whose centres lie within 0.15 of p. Move each of them away from p by 0.01 along the line from p to its centre. Give the reinserted circle an initial radius of 0.01 instead of 0. Then run _optimise, clip, repair, and accept if the sum improves. Starting from a slightly infeasible point with an open pocket helps SLSQP actually grow the new circle, where a zero-radius circle tends to stay degenerate.
backlog.title: Reinsert with a small positive radius and jitter neighbours

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the uniform random initial centres with a mixture of k = 3 to 5 Gaussian clusters: draw cluster centres uniformly in [0.2, 0.8]^2, then draw each of the n centres from a normal with standard deviation 0.15 around a randomly chosen cluster centre, and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Keep the radii initialisation at INIT_RADIUS and all other code unchanged. The point is to vary density across restarts rather than always sampling a flat distribution.
backlog.title: Gaussian-cluster initial centres for random restarts

backlog.spec: At the end of the restart phase keep the top 3 distinct packings by sum. In the reinsertion loop cycle through the 3 elites, applying the remove-and-reinsert step to each in turn and replacing that elite only on improvement. Return the best at the end. This spreads the search across several basins at no extra cost per step.
backlog.title: Round-robin over top-3 elites

backlog.spec: Change RESTART_FRACTION from 0.3 to 0.15, so that more of the 24 s budget goes to the remove-and-reinsert loop. That loop is where the incumbent gains most. Keep the guard that at least one restart runs. Change nothing else. This is a one-line schedule change that should be replicated twice.
backlog.title: Shorter restart phase, longer reinsertion phase

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, keep an integer k starting at 0. At each step remove the circle with the (k mod n)-th smallest radius (np.argsort(r)[k % n]) instead of always the smallest, reinsert it at a uniform random position with radius 0 and re-solve as now. If the candidate improves the sum of radii, accept it and reset k to 0. Otherwise, increment a failure counter; after every 3 consecutive failures at the same rank, increase k by 1 and reset the counter. This makes the loop move on to larger circles when the smallest one is stuck. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Escalating removal rank after failed reinsertions

memo: Helped: slot 0 (remove-smallest-and-reinsert after a short random-restart phase) is the incumbent at -2.6311 (runs -2.6305, -2.6316; delta -0.0031). Several replicated variants sit near or below the incumbent but were rejected: slot 18 annealing acceptance (-2.6348/-2.6332), slot 4 Latin hypercube starts (-2.6343/-2.6335), slot 30 hex/uniform alternation (-2.6337/-2.6317), slot 34 multi-removal (-2.6334/-2.6313). Their deltas are within noise of slot 0 and may be worse or equal. Slot 32 analytic gradients (-2.6330, one run) and slot 7 log-normal radii (-2.6325, one run) are unreliable at noise sd 0.0023. Did not help: basin hopping (+0.0030), position screening (+0.0023), sparse constraints (+0.0021), ring starts (+0.0037), mirror starts (+0.0036), squeeze (+0.0015); most other tweaks about +-0.0002. Next: combine slot 0 with LHS starts, the slot 18 acceptance rule and analytic gradients (faster SLSQP), replicate at least twice, then add the slot 7 radii init. Avoid single-run conclusions.
